packs.title: Philosophy Starter Pack
packs.description: Short long-form pieces designed to slow down impulse and sharpen intent.

items.title: The Quiet Hours
items.description: Most of what we remember about our own lives happens in the margins — the hours no one was watching, including us. What we call attention is usually the absence of its opposite.

items.title: How Bees Decide
items.description: A single scout bee returns to the hive with news of a flower. What happens next is a small democracy — one that turns out to look remarkably like human deliberation.

items.title: A Letter About Rain
items.description: My grandmother kept a rain journal. Thirty-one years of weather in tidy columns. It was the most useful and the most useless book I have ever read.

items.title: The Map Is Not the City
items.description: Urban designers draw with certainty. Residents live with doubt. The gap between the two is where a city either becomes habitable or doesn't.

packs.title: Science Starter Pack
packs.description: Calmer, knowledge-dense reads that can substitute for impulsive opens.

items.title: How product loops borrow from reward prediction
items.description: A science-forward explanation of why intermittent reward keeps users checking.

items.title: Why tiny commitments beat heroic intention
items.description: A compact behavior-science read about why a short replacement often wins.

items.title: Designing for curiosity without designing addiction
items.description: A product essay on making discovery finite instead of compulsive.
